item.title: Economics of Prevention, Health Behaviors, and Equity
item.content:encoded:
Contributions apply microeconometric methods to the analysis of the economics of prevention, health behaviors, and equity. In particular, these concern the study of lifestyle choices, the demand for health care, or more specific topics such as vaccination uptake, risk preferences, or health literacy.

From a methodological perspective, submissions especially encourage the employment of modern tools of causal inference and exploitation of behavioral interventions, public health programs, or other policy measures.

Submissions should mainly examine individual decision-making in well-defined institutional or policy contexts and aim to generate insights that are relevant both academically and for policy.

Potential topics

  • Microeconometric methods applied to the economics of prevention, health behaviors, and equity
  • Lifestyle choices and demand for health care
  • Vaccination uptake and risk preferences
  • Health literacy studies
  • Causal inference methods in health economics
  • Behavioral interventions and public health programs
  • Policy measures evaluation
  • Individual decision-making in institutional and policy contexts

item.title: Grounded in Causality: Elevating Evidence for Leadership Practice
item.content:encoded:
This special issue of The Leadership Quarterly seeks empirical research that advances our understanding of leadership through rigorous causal inference methods. We invite submissions that employ experimental designs, quasi-experimental approaches, longitudinal studies, or other methodologically sound approaches to establish causal relationships in leadership phenomena.

Timeline

  • November 22, 2026: Full paper submission deadline
